Kernel 6.20 Released

The Linux 6.20 kernel was released today with broad hardware enablement and improved power management for recent laptops. The release closes a long development cycle and lands several scheduler refinements.

Maintainers highlighted a long-awaited filesystem fix, better support for newer GPUs, and a series of patches that reduce idle power draw on mobile hardware. Distributions are expected to ship the update over the coming weeks.

Reviewers cautioned that some out-of-tree modules still need updates before the kernel is widely deployed in production environments.
